stories.title: Four arrested over boxing champion's murder in South Africa
stories.summary: Four people have been arrested in South Africa in connection with the murder of boxing champion Zolani Tete, who was shot dead outside his home on Friday. Tete, 38, was gunned down in what has been described as an ambush in Mdantsane, Eastern Cape. A young woman who was with him was also shot and is in hospital. One of the men being held, a 22-year-old who was arrested on Saturday, will make an initial appearance in court on Monday, and faces murder and attempted murder charges. Tete held the WBO bantamweight title from 2017 to 2019, as well as the IBF super-flyweight title in 2014. He was later given a four-year ban, which lapsed in July this year. The remaining suspects, who were arrested on Sunday, are due in court on Tuesday. Two have been charged with unlawful possession of firearms and ammunition. It is unclear whether they will also be charged with murder and attempted murder. Tete was in his car waiting for the gate to his house to open when two armed suspects in balaclavas emerged from a vehicle and fired "multiple shots" at him and a 27‑year‑old female passenger, according to officials. Tributes have been pouring in for the two-time world champion since his death. South Africa's Sports Minister Gayton McKenzie said: "South Africa has lost one of the finest fighters it has ever produced."

stories.title: Nearly 90,000 told to evacuate as wildfire approaches Reno, Nevada
stories.summary: Tens of thousands of people have been told to evacuate from an area close to Reno, Nevada, as a large wildfire reached the outskirts of the city. Around 42,000 people have been ordered to leave their homes immediately, with a further 45,000 people urged to get ready to leave. The fire, which was first reported on Saturday morning, had so far injured six people, officials said. Windy and unpredictable weather conditions have contributed to its spread. Nevada's Governor Joe Lombardo has declared a state of emergency in Washoe County and ordered the National Guard to join firefighting and law enforcement efforts. "This is an active and rapidly evolving situation and I urge everyone in the affected areas to remain vigilant and follow the direction of local officials," he said. The fire was caused by humans and first reported at 11:15 local time (18:15 GMT) on Saturday, according to local officials. They said that, as of Sunday evening, the fire had burned around 10,500 acres and was 0% contained. Around 13,700 homes were inside the evacuation area, local emergency services said, with two shelters set up to take in displaced residents. Of the six injured, three were emergency responders fighting the fire. All Washoe County schools will be closed on Monday, except one, and mass road closures are in place. Reno, in western Nevada, is located close to the state boundary with California and has a population of around 280,000 people.

stories.title: Canada vows to impose retaliatory tariffs against the U.S.
stories.summary: Canada is vowing to impose fresh tariffs on US goods in retaliation for Trump administration taxes. The moves come after talks between the two trading partners broke down late last week.

stories.title: Western NGOs implicated in attempts to destabilize Russia ahead of elections — legislator
stories.summary: Vasily Piskarev highlighted that personnel from Western NGOs were engaged in training provocateurs to be used the electoral period
article_sentences: MOSCOW, August 24.

The State Duma’s Commission for Investigating Foreign Interference in Russia’s Internal Affairs has determined that Western non-governmental organizations are actively attempting to destabilize Russia ahead of the upcoming elections, according to commission head Vasily Piskarev.
"Western NGOs are involved in efforts to undermine stability within Russia in connection with the forthcoming elections," Piskarev stated.
He further explained that certain "human rights" organizations operating in Russia possess materials containing disparaging assessments of Russian electoral laws and the electoral process itself.

Additionally, some analytical websites have issued calls to "destabilize the system through regional and municipal levels," alongside proposals to escalate Ukrainian attacks against Russia prior to the vote.
Piskarev also highlighted that personnel from other NGOs, such as the US-based Human Rights Foundation, are engaged in training provocateurs to be used the electoral period.

In response, he welcomed the recent decision by the Prosecutor General’s Office, which supported the commission’s recommendation and declared the activities of the Human Rights Foundation undesirable within Russia.
